response.message:
I've drawn the full IBM Cloud setup for answering questions from the synthetic documents. A small ingestion job loads documents, their access rules and revisions into Cloudant. A Code Engine RAG service checks the user's App ID token, runs keyword search only over documents they're allowed to see, calls watsonx.ai and shows citations. Our first local test will use synthetic users and a scripted (mocked) model to check the access-control, citation, abstention, update and revocation logic. That proves the control flow only: whether a real watsonx.ai model answers well, and whether we have access to it in a given region, is still unverified until we test against the real service. None of these IBM boxes has a generator yet, so they remain engineering work.

Which country do the data and users need to stay in? For example, Germany or the US.

proposal.title: IBM Cloud bounded keyword RAG – end-to-end sketch
proposal.body: Full path: operator ingestion → COS → Code Engine ingestion job → Cloudant catalog (docs, ACLs, revisions); user → web app → App ID sign-in → RAG API (ACL filter, keyword retrieval, revision recheck, abstention, revocation check) → watsonx.ai. Assumptions: region, account, model access and plans are unverified. There is no native IBM generator for these components, so they are design-only with engineering gaps. Local tests use mocked model responses.

data.label: Content operator
data.description: Loads synthetic documents with explicit ACLs. Outside provisioning scope.

data.label: Source documents
data.description: Private bucket for synthetic UTF-8 documents and ACL manifests. Versioning lets updates and deletions be detected.

data.label: Ingestion job
data.description: Reads changed objects, then writes document text, keyword terms, ACLs and revision IDs to the catalog using conditional writes. Applies deletions as tombstones.

data.label: RAG catalog
data.description: Bounded catalog of 100 documents or fewer: content, keyword index, explicit ACLs and current revisions. It is the source of truth for permission and revision rechecks.

data.label: Employee browser
data.description: A signed-in user asking questions. Client reference, not provisioned.

data.label: Web application
data.description: Authenticated chat UI. Shows the cited answer or an abstention. Signs in through App ID with authorization code + PKCE.

data.label: Identity
data.description: User sign-in with MFA. Issues the tokens that the RAG API validates. Unknown identities fail closed.

data.label: RAG API
data.description: Validates the token, filters by ACL before retrieval, runs bounded keyword search and sends only permitted passages to the model. Abstains when support is insufficient, rechecks ACLs/revisions after generation and suppresses the answer if access was revoked. Returns citations with revision IDs.

data.label: Model runtime
data.description: Foundation-model inference for grounded answers. The model ID, regional availability and entitlement are not yet verified. Local tests use mocked responses.

data.label: Audit & logs
data.description: Request, denial, abstention and revocation-suppression events, with no document text.

requirementDrafts.basis: "Known questions cite current source revisions; Unsupported questions abstain"
requirementDrafts.statement: Answers to known questions must cite the current source revisions, and unsupported questions must abstain.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Without freshness and post-generation rechecks, removed or revoked content still reaches users.
requirementDrafts.basis: "Updates and deletions change retrieval; Revocation during generation suppresses the answer"
requirementDrafts.statement: Updates and deletions must change retrieval results, and access revoked during generation must suppress the answer.

response.message:
No checks ran, so nothing passed yet. The design isn't validated. All 8 blockers have the same cause: there's no IBM generator yet for the ingestion job, the Cloudant catalog, App ID, or the two Code Engine apps, and the two existing actors still need a reference plan. That's product engineering work, not a mistake in your diagram. I won't shrink the design to just Cloud Object Storage storage to make the check pass, because that would drop all five of your acceptance criteria.

The bounded keyword RAG contract with these checks exists only for AWS today, so there's a decision to make. Should we keep IBM and log these 8 gaps as engineering work, with the AWS contract reproducer as the spec? Or do you want an AWS reference copy as a parallel experiment, so the access-control and revocation logic can be emulated now, with IBM staying your accepted platform?
